notable_claims: System administrators should not intervene in disputes regarding the internal management or moderation of specific newsgroups.
classification.summary: A system administrator at the University of Massachusetts Boston responded to requests for disciplinary action against a user involved in a controversy within the soc.religion.islam newsgroup. The administrator declined to intervene, stating that it is not the role of network administration to judge newsgroup management or moderator procedures.
classification.title: Controversy in soc.religion.islam and news admin policy

identity.subject: Controversy in soc.religion.islam and news admin policy

notable_claims: System administrators are not responsible for judging the fairness of newsgroup moderator procedures.
University system access should not be revoked based on content disputes unless gross technical violations (e.g., mail-bombing) occur.
classification.summary: Elizabeth Schwartz, a system administrator at UMass Boston, responds to requests for action against user Ahmed Hashem regarding a dispute in the soc.religion.islam newsgroup. She asserts that the university will not intervene in newsgroup management disputes or moderator procedures. The post emphasizes that users have the right to resolve their own conflicts as long as they do not violate system-level technical etiquette.
classification.title: Controversy in soc.religion.islam and news admin policy

notable_claims: Professor Jennifer Bankier advocated for a speech code based on the claim that she was not free to speak as a woman.
classification.summary: This post discusses a debate over the implementation of a speech code at Dalhousie University in Canada. It specifically critiques Professor Jennifer Bankier's claim that she lacked free speech as a woman, contrasting this with her positions of power within the university.
classification.title: Speech Code at Dalhousie U. (Canada)

notable_claims: The imposition of a speech code is described as a declaration of educational failure.
Speech codes are claimed to encourage anonymous complaints and secret disciplinary procedures over open intellectual confrontation.
classification.summary: A column by Parker Barss Donham criticizes the Dalhousie University Senate's decision to establish a code against discriminatory harassment. Donham argues that speech codes are an educational failure that protect students from necessary intellectual conflict rather than equipping them to confront bigotry. He contrasts the proposed code with an example of students at Arizona State University who used open dialogue and activism to combat racist flyers.
classification.title: Speech Code at Dalhousie U. (Canada)

classification.summary: Carl Kadie requested permission from Parker Barss Donham to repost a column regarding speech codes. Donham granted the request for the content to be shared on alt.comp.acad-freedom.talk/news.
classification.title: Re: Repost permission request

notable_claims: The University of Waterloo banned five Internet newsgroups on February 1, 1994.
The UW GSA Board of Directors formally resolved to petition the administration for their reinstatement.
classification.summary: The Graduate Student Association (GSA) at the University of Waterloo passed a motion to initiate a petition demanding the reinstatement of five banned Internet newsgroups. The ban had been implemented by the university administration on February 1, 1994. This action represents student-led opposition to administrative censorship of network communications.

notable_claims: The University of Waterloo Ethics Committee banned alt.tasteless, alt.sex.stories, and alt.sex.stories.d.
University legal counsel did not recommend the removal of these newsgroups.
classification.summary: The University of Waterloo Ethics Committee banned access to specific Usenet newsgroups, including alt.tasteless and alt.sex.stories. This action was taken despite the university's legal counsel not recommending the removal of these groups. The committee justified the ban on the basis that the groups might occasionally contain obscene material.
classification.title: UW censorship - where does it end? Is Gopher to be censored?

notable_claims: The newsgroup 'alt.tasteless' was banned from University of Waterloo campus computers starting February 1, 1994.
University legal counsel specifically recommended removing alt.sex.bondage and alt.sex.bestiality but not alt.tasteless.
classification.summary: Jeffrey Shallit disputes the justification for banning the newsgroup 'alt.tasteless' at the University of Waterloo. He claims that while the university cited legal counsel as a basis for the ban, the counsel only recommended removing groups related to bondage and bestiality. According to Shallit, the Ethics Committee independently decided to censor 'alt.tasteless' based on the possibility that it might contain obscene material.
classification.title: UW censorship - where does it end? Is Gopher to be censored?
